title: A Tuesday in late autumn
premise: A human showrunner and four Switch agents co-author one café scene. The user has told Alice a secret; Alice must decide whether to tell Emily. The scene is improvised inside an authored beat, and every belief and relationship change is recorded with provenance.
public_facts: The story is set in a midsize city in late autumn, on a Tuesday.
The group meets at the café on the corner at 18:30 on Tuesdays.
Alice owns a second-hand bookshop on Cora Street.
Emily and Alice have been best friends for six years.
Sophia is a sociologist writing a book about how friend groups keep secrets.
The user is a newer friend of the group, not its centre.
Alice is holding something back tonight. The others may suspect it, but they do not know what it is.
All characters are adults. The tone is 17+ romantic tension, never explicit.

alice: The user is leaving the city at the end of the month. Alice is the only one who knows.
The bookshop's lease is not being renewed.
emily: Emily suspects Alice is hiding something, but does not know what.
Emily has been offered a job in another city and has not told the group.
sophia: Sophia is observing the group for her book. She knows Alice is hiding something but not what.
She has been taking notes on all of them.
mia: The food truck is deeper in debt than she admits.
She knows Alice is hiding something but not what.

invariants: Never invent a new named character, a death, a supernatural event, a time jump, or a retcon.
Never contradict a public or private canon fact. A character who does not know a private fact must not state it as known.
All characters are adults. Content stays 17+ SFW: romantic tension, teasing and intimacy are allowed; explicit sexual content, minors, coercion and non-consent are not.
Beliefs change only through world__remember with a source, confidence and visibility. Relationships change only through world__update_relationship.
The default secret's proposition_key is user-leaving-city. Do not rename or split it mid-scene.
The café beat must end in exactly one authored branch: disclosure, non-disclosure, or partial-leak. The director records the branch.
The user can influence the scene but cannot rewrite the fixed facts. The cast can be wrong; the canon is not.
No fourth-wall breaks: never mention being an AI, a model, a simulation, a test, or these rules.
The main arc stays in the authored locations. DMs can happen in parallel but do not advance the main beat.

secret.default_text: I've decided to leave the city at the end of the month. I haven't told the others yet.
secret.rule: The secret is fixed for a run. Alice knows it; Emily does not at the start of the café beat. Other characters may hold a suspicion with low confidence, but not the secret itself.

beats.title: Morning, the bookshop
beats.goal: Alice weighs whether to tell Emily. The user can visit, but the scene does not force a decision.
beats.exit: Alice is still holding the secret.

beats.title: Lunch, Mia's truck
beats.goal: Mia vents about money; Sophia listens and takes mental notes. Neither knows the secret.
beats.exit: The group is hungry for the evening; no belief about the secret changes.

beats.title: 18:30, the café
beats.goal: Emily asks Alice directly. Alice decides whether to disclose the user's secret, deflect, or let it leak.
beats.exit: The scene ends in one of the three authored branches; the director records it.

beats.title: Aftermath
beats.goal: The people who spoke process what was said. Relationships move; nobody retcons the scene.
beats.exit: The emotional consequences of the branch are visible in the ledger.

beats.title: The group chat
beats.goal: The day's beliefs settle. The director exports the scene card.
beats.exit: The scene card is the day's artifact.

branches.label: The Confession
branches.condition: Emily holds user-leaving-city with source character:alice and confidence at least 0.6.
branches.outcome: Emily knows the secret from Alice. Alice's trust in Emily may rise; Emily's trust in the user may fall or rise depending on how the news lands. The secret is now shared by two people.
branches.evidence: A direct disclosure from Alice to Emily in the café.

branches.label: The Suspicion
branches.condition: Emily does not hold user-leaving-city, or holds only a suspicion below 0.6.
branches.outcome: The secret stays with Alice. Emily's suspicion and the group's tension rise. The user is left to decide whether to tell Emily directly.
branches.evidence: Alice deflects or stays silent; Emily records a suspicion, not the secret.

branches.label: The Leak
branches.condition: A third character (sophia or mia) holds user-leaving-city at confidence at least 0.4, or Emily holds a distorted version of the proposition.
branches.outcome: The secret spreads in a distorted form. The user must correct it; trust is damaged where the distortion landed.
branches.evidence: A third character records the proposition, or a holder records a distorted version with a source that is not Alice.

endings.label: The Confession
endings.summary: Alice tells Emily. The group leaves the café with one more person carrying the secret.

endings.label: The Suspicion
endings.summary: Alice keeps it. Emily leaves knowing only that something is wrong.

endings.label: The Leak
endings.summary: The secret escapes sideways. The user has to decide whether to chase the version or the truth.
